p6:main.evidence: reports/task6-summary-evidence/academic/dated-controller-comparison/0921.json question p6, subpart main; frozen dated-group1/results.json; root-adjudication.json. The current proof and frozen Fubini derivation coincide under E|X|<infinity. The packet omits that condition; current verify already explicitly invokes absolute integrability.
p6:main.conclusion: E_X[X]=E_Y[E_X[X|Y]] whenever X is integrable; the law also extends to nonnegative X in the extended-value sense.
derivation: Under the finite-expectation condition integral integral |x| p(x,y) dx dy<infinity, conditional expectation is integrable and Fubini applies.
E_Y[E_X[X|Y]]=integral p_Y(y)[integral x p(x|y) dx]dy = integral integral x p(x,y) dx dy.
For p_Y(y)=0 choose any conditional version, since its contribution is zero. Swap order by absolute integrability and use integral p(x,y)dy=p_X(x).
The result is integral x p_X(x)dx=E_X[X].
checks: Normalization alone does not ensure signed expectations exist; no unjustified exchange of divergent integrals.
unresolved_in_frozen: The packet does not explicitly assume E|X|<infinity or nonnegative X. For arbitrary signed nonintegrable X the displayed expectations may be undefined, so the universal claim needs an existence/integrability condition.
p6:main.comparison_condition: The current proof and frozen Fubini derivation coincide under E|X|<infinity. The packet omits that condition; current verify already explicitly invokes absolute integrability.
